study: Window threshold: offer quality on the same cases, and search efficiency under load
scheduler: local compose, Omaha routing, booking publish fix
protocol: Quality: per profile, 2 schedules optimized with daily proposals, each with 20 job addresses searched once per threshold (2,25,1000) in a rotated order; the best offer confirmed and priced with routes/evaluate, never written. Efficiency: 120 s cold-address booking runs at thresholds 2, 25, 1000, 1 and 5 desks, 1 repeats, interleaved. Profiles: low (1 visit a day per technician) and high (2 visits a day, the first 12 weekdays at 4), with 5, 10, 20, 30 technicians each. Fixed 10 weekdays throughout.
hypotheses: Thresholds between 2 and 1000 stay inert on these schedules at every fleet size: a regular window is a date and time, counted once however many technicians could take it, so a 13-date horizon has more than 25 whatever the fleet.
The insertion pass grows with the fleet, so the threshold-2 search median at 1 desk rises with technicians (about 0.35 s at 6), staying inside the 5 s deadline at 30.
The 250 ms refinement cap covers a smaller share of a bigger fleet, so the gap between thresholds 2 and 1000 in best-offer cost widens with technicians; at 6 it was under a dollar a booking.
At threshold 1000 the complete refinement grows with the fleet until the 5 s deadline stops it: from about 20 technicians even 1 desk answers searchComplete false.
